sources.read: Full collection text read on 2026-11-14; stated image/plan also inspected where recorded.
confirmed: Register-based account distinguishes open/half-decked and later decked states.
A small fore-deck cuddy is described for crew sleeping on the earlier vessel.
application: Establishes the modest scale of a crew cuddy; no fixed berth plan is documented for this game family. Our aft bench/locker cuddy is authored to match the preserved quarterdeck, not Ada’s fore-cuddy.

plan: Large uncluttered working hold -0.30L to +0.37L, floor -0.80 m, cargo laid beside a central aisle.
Small after cuddy -0.47L to -0.33L, sunk sole -0.30 m, bench and locker, with no freestanding adult berth; no saloon table suite.
2.0 × 1.35 m main hatch at +0.12L, low quarterdeck companion and visible ladder/stair.
Twelve open-battery guns, low bulwarks, compact capstan with messenger rope, and actual fitted planked cargo boxes.
limitations: Later Cornish fishing records constrain accommodation scale, not the chronology or exact rig of the game asset.
Cargo assortment and compartment dimensions are authored.

The authored narrow aft cuddy cannot support a freestanding 0.60 × 1.80 m adult berth while retaining its 0.65 m aisle, supported sole and real descending companion. The read source establishes a modest cuddy but no fixed berth arrangement for this game family; bench and locker are inferred without extending the cabin into the battery.
The actual narrow supported hold accepts planked cargo boxes; no unmodeled cargo casks or separate rope coils are claimed.

The modest aft casements use proportionate segmented timber jambs that follow the actual tapered reveal, leaving every retained glass pane clear through the hull opening. The exact glazing arrangement is an authored fitting choice informed by small timber-vessel construction, not an inspected plan of this proprietary game interior.
